text:
sanjay: heads-up — running into a weird stack when trying to run the node/ts SDK in a Next edge function with streaming enabled. ESM import works in node but in the edge runtime the auth header is missing intermittently. SDK v0.12.3
marta: ugh. can you paste the minimal handler and how you're bundling? next/vite?
sanjay: Next 14 edge, `runtime: 'edge'`, using the app router. build target is edge, and the SDK is imported like: `import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'`. no extra polyfills.
ev an: are you using the edge entrypoint (`module` field) or the cjs build accidentally? sometimes bundlers pick `main` over `module`.
sanjay: i think next is resolving to the ESM entry but the produced bundle still includes a tiny polyfill that rewrites Headers. auth shows up as `Authorization` on server logs but inside the SDK request it's blank.
tanya: do you have any middleware rewriting fetch or the global Request/Headers? we had an issue where a telemetry lib replaced `Headers.prototype.append` and broke header propagation in ReadableStream pipes.
sanjay: good point — i checked, no monkeypatches. small reproduction attached below:```js
// app/api/gen/route.ts (edge)
export const runtime = 'edge'
import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY })
export default async function handler(req) {
  const stream = await client.stream({ prompt: 'hi' })
  return new Response(stream.body)
}
```
marta: do you call `stream()` which uses an internal `fetch`? if the SDK builds with `node-fetch` polyfill it might be swapping behavior. for edge you need to make sure the bundle uses web fetch, not node polyfills.
jeamie: quick tip — in next, set `experimental.externalDir` or add package to `transpilePackages` sometimes helps so the bundler doesn't wrap it. also check `next.config.js` `webpack` fallbacks.
ev an: also note that Vite sometimes replaces `global`/`process` causing auth-checks that read `process.env` at build time to be empty. for edge ensure env is injected at runtime or passed by server.
sanjay: tried `transpilePackages: ['@redwood/inference']` — still same. headers show up in Vercel logs but inside `client.stream()` the request going out to model server has no Authorization header.
tanya: can you log inside the SDK? maybe `client._opts` or debug flag?
sanjay: debug helped — the SDK creates a `Request` from `new Request(url, { headers })` then does `fetch(req)`. The headers object was an instance of the platform `Headers` but all values are empty strings. very odd.
marta: this rings a bell. we had an edge case where `Headers` values got coerced due to `Object.freeze` on the headers object during bundling step. bundlers sometimes hoist objects and freeze them. if headers were frozen earlier, appending works but getting value returns ''.
jeamie: workaround: construct headers inline in the fetch call: `fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + key } })` instead of `new Headers(...)` or clone before passing.
ev an: longer term, SDK should detect edge env and avoid creating `Headers` when running under `globalThis.fetch` presence. we should publish a tiny patch.
tanya: also confirm you aren't shipping the node-only build — add `exports` resolution check in package.json to ensure `./edge` entrypoint for web runtimes.
sanjay: thanks. any quick patch i can apply to our app while the SDK is fixed?
marta: simplest: create your own wrapper around the SDK stream call to inject the header directly in the `fetch` options. e.g.:
```js
// wrapper to force header in fetch options
const originalFetch = globalThis.fetch
globalThis.fetch = (input, init = {}) => {
  init = { ...init, headers: { ...(init.headers || {}), Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.RW_API_KEY}` } }
  return originalFetch(input, init)
}
```
sanjay: ok i'll try that as a hotfix. does anyone know if this affects Vite SSR or only Next edge?
jeamie: Vite SSR can also be affected if adapter or bundler inlines/freeze-shakes objects. behavior differs across adapters. Next edge is more strict.
ev an: for streaming quirks, remember the edge runtime expects `ReadableStream` or `Response`—if SDK returns a Node stream, the adapter will polyfill and can strip headers. ensure the SDK exposes a web-stream in edge builds.
sanjay: last q — auth retries: if a 401 happens, SDK retries with exponential backoff, but on edge we saw 2x requests (duplicate tokens) — is that expected?
marta: retry should be idempotent for token refresh flows. on edge, avoid retries that replay streaming bodies. SDK should do a preflight token check for streaming endpoints. we'll file an issue.
tanya: logging for this thread: filed internal issue INF-2743 and assigned to eng-runtime. devex-bot please link.
devex-bot: Issue created: https://internal.redwood/INF-2743 \"edge headers missing in SDK streaming on Next edge\" — assigned to @eng-runtime, priority P2 :white_check_mark:
sanjay: thanks all, i'll ship the wrapper hotfix and report back with logs. really appreciate the quick triage :thumbsup:
